title: Polish deputies at Thorn: justify and sanctify together
source_text: XXI. Hanc autem esse genuinam Doctorum Ecclesiae Reformatae sententiam dubitare non possunt qui eorum scripta candide expenderunt, ut innumeris eorum testimoniis manifestum fieri possit. Instar multorum esse debet quod protestantur hac de re Reformatorum in regno Poloniae deputati, in declaratione suae sententiae, quam in Thoruniensi conventu obtulerunt. Ibi enim capite quarto, quod est de Gratia, dicunt Deum vocatos & sincere resipiscentes, non tantum propter solum Christi meritum ex mera gratia imputatum, a peccatis justificare, seu absolvere, & in filios adoptare; sed simul etiam spiritu charitatis in corda nostra effuso, ad syncerum sanctimoniae & obedientiae novae studium in dies magis magisque renovare, & sanctificare, seu justos & sanctos facere.
pass_a_gloss: That this is the genuine judgment of the doctors of the Reformed church those cannot doubt who have candidly weighed their writings, as can be made plain by countless testimonies of theirs. Standing for many should be what the deputies of the Reformers in the kingdom of Poland protest on this matter in the declaration of their judgment which they offered in the Thorn colloquy. There in chapter four, which is on Grace, they say that God not only justifies—that is, absolves—and adopts into sons those called and sincerely repentant for the sake of Christ’s merit alone imputed from mere grace, but at the same time also, by the Spirit of charity poured into our hearts, renews them more and more day by day to a sincere pursuit of holiness and new obedience, and sanctifies them—that is, makes them just and holy.
pass_b_english: Thorn Polish declaration: for Christ’s alone-imputed merit God absolves and adopts.
At once by poured-out charity he renews and sanctifies unto new obedience.
